chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from one of his companions, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there are three hours in the night and three hours in the day in which He glorifies Himself. So the first of the hours of the day is when the sun is on this side, meaning from the east, its measure is from Al-'Asr, meaning from the west, up to the first Salat; and the first of the hours of the night is in the remaining third of the night, up to when the dawn breaks.

He says: 'I am Allah, Lord of the worlds. I am Allah, the Almighty, the Wise. I am Allah, the Forgiving, the Merciful. I am Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. I am Allah, the Master of the Day of Judgment. I am Allah, I have not ceased and will not cease. I am Allah, Creator of good and evil. I am Allah, Creator of Paradise and Fire. I am Allah, the Originator of all things, and to Me is the return. I am Allah, the One, the Eternal. I am Allah, the Knower of the unseen and the seen. I am Allah, the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Believer, the Guardian, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Majestic. I am Allah, the Creator, the Evolver, the Fashioner. For Me are the Good Names. I am Allah, the Great, the Exalted.'
He said, then Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said from himself: 'And Greatness is His Robe, so whoever competes with Him for any part of that, Allah will cast him into the Fire.'

Then he said: 'There is no believing servant who supplicates with these, with his heart facing Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that Allah fulfills his need, and if he was unfortunate, I hope he will be transformed into a fortunate one.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific times for Allah's glorification and what is the reward for supplicating with His names?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the concept of 'Istifrad' (self-glorification) at specific canonical times, linking divine majesty with the exclusive right to greatness (Al-Kibriya). It serves as a theological basis for the belief that Allah's greatness is unique, warning against any claim of equality, while promising the fulfillment of needs for believers who recite these attributes with a focused heart.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘For Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic there are four timings during the night, and three timings during the day in which Heazwj Glorifies Himselfazwj. So the first timing of the day is when the sun happens to be on this side, meaning from the east its measurement from Al-Asr, meaning from the west, up to the first Salat; and the first timing of the night during the remaining third from the night up to the morning breaking forth.

He<sup>azwj</sup> is Saying: 
“I<sup>azwj</sup> am Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the worlds. I<sup>azwj</sup> am Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the Mighty, the Wise! I<sup>azwj</sup> am Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the Forgiver, the Merciful! I<sup>azwj</sup> am Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the Beneficent, the Merficul! I<sup>azwj</sup> am Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the Master of the Day of the Religion (Judgment). I<sup>asws</sup> Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, I<sup>azwj</sup> neither do I<sup>azwj</sup> decline nor will I<sup>azwj</sup> cease to be. I<sup>azwj</sup> am Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Creator of the good and the evil. I<sup>azwj</sup> am Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Creator of the Paradise and the Fire. I<sup>azwj</sup> am Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the Initiator of everything, to Me<sup>azwj</sup> it would all return. 
I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> am Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, the Alone, the Last. I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> am Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> the Knower of the unseen and the seen. I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> am Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> the King, the Holy, the Source of safety, the Securor, the Controller, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Supreme. I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> am Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> the Creator, the Evolver, the Designer. For Me<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> are the Good Names. I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> am Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, the Greatest, the Exalted”’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said from himself<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>: ‘And the Greatness is His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Robe, so the one who snatches anything from that, Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Fling him into the Fire’.

Then heasws said: ‘There is none from a Momin servant who supplicates with these being attentive with his heart towards Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic, except his need would be Fulfilled, and if he was unfortunate, hoping, he would be transformed to be a fortunate one’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Safwan ibn Y ahya from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from certain individuals of his people from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“In three hours of the day and in three hours of the night Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, glorifies Himself. The first hours of the day begin when the distance of the sun from this side, the East, is equal to that between ‘Asr (the beginning of afternoon prayer), on the West, and the start of the time of the first prayer (prayer at noon time), and the first hours of night which begin with the start of the remaining one third of the night to dawn.

“Allah says, ‘I am Allah, Cherisher of the worlds, I am Allah, the Most High, the Most Great, I am Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Wise, I am Allah, the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful, I am Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful, I am Allah, the Owner of the Day of Judgment, I am Allah, Who has always been and will be, I am Allah, the Creator of the good and bad, I am Allah, the Creator of paradise and fire, I am Allah, the Initiator of all things and to Me it returns, I am Allah, the only One and Self-sufficient, I am Allah, the Knower of the unseen and the seen, I am Allah, the Owner, the Holy, the Peace, the Protector, the Dominant, the Compeller, the One who is Proud, I am Allah, the Creator, the Designer, and the Shape-giver. 1 have all good names; I am Allah, the Great and the Most Lofty. ’
“The narrator has said that abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) then said in his own words, ‘Greatness is His dress. Whoever disputes Him in that, He (Allah) will throw him in fire.’

The Imam then said, ‘Whoever of the believing people prays to Him in these words turning with his heart to Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, He will grant his wish. Even if he is a person of evil fortune, I hope he will change into a person of good fortune.’”
